drafted_from: tool:make-a-lut-for-log-footage row in tool-rows.json, do-work/make_lut.py and test/make-lut.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "My flat log footage from the made-up Orchard camera looks grey; make me a LUT with its profile in orchard.profile.json, 33 points a side, saved as orchard.cube." It writes the .cube file on your computer and names the settings it used.
no_lists_because: It names no list: it reads one profile JSON file you give it and writes one .cube file, keeping nothing else.
instructions: 1. Get the camera's profile: a JSON record of kind log-to-display-profile holding its log curve, gamut matrix, luma weights, video range, shoulder and display gamma (your AI can read yours, or build one from the maker's published log curve); write it to a file.
2. Install numpy once (python3 -m pip install -U numpy) and clone the Workshop repository.

3. Say "Make a LUT for this footage" and name the profile and the output; your AI reads the row with tools:list and runs `python3 -I tools/make-a-lut-for-log-footage/do-work/make_lut.py --profile <profile> --out <file>.cube`, adding --exposure, --saturation, --size, --red-gain or --blue-gain if you ask.

4. Read the last line: {"result": {"lut", "profile", "size", "entries", "exposure", "saturation", "red_gain", "blue_gain"}} names the file and settings; {"error": "what to change"} says what the profile lacks. Put the .cube in the editor's or ffmpeg's LUT step for footage of that camera and curve only.

worked_examples.title: A made-up camera's profile becomes a 9-point table
worked_examples.ask: Make a LUT for my Orchard camera's log footage, small, 9 points a side.
worked_examples.given: From tools/make-a-lut-for-log-footage/test/make-lut.test.mjs: the command line is `python3 -I tools/make-a-lut-for-log-footage/do-work/make_lut.py --profile made-up.json --out lut.cube --size 9`. made-up.json is {"kind": "log-to-display-profile", "title": "Made-up camera log to display", "log_curve": {"code_scale": 255, "cut_code": 60, "log": {"base": 2, "offset_code": 120, "slope_code": 40, "mid_grey": 0.2, "pedestal": 0.02}, "toe": {"origin_code": 20, "linear_at_cut": 0.02}}, "gamut_matrix": [[1.2, -0.1, -0.1], [-0.05, 1.1, -0.05], [0, -0.1, 1.1]], "luma_weights": [0.3, 0.59, 0.11], "video_range": {"black_code": 16, "white_code": 235}, "shoulder": {"a": 2.4, "b": 0.05, "c": 2.4, "d": 0.6, "e": 0.15}, "display_gamma": 2.2}.
worked_examples.hands_back: The last line printed is {"result": {"lut": "lut.cube", "profile": "Made-up camera log to display", "size": 9, "entries": 729, "exposure": 1.0, "saturation": 1.0, "red_gain": 1.0, "blue_gain": 1.0}}. lut.cube starts with the lines TITLE "Made-up camera log to display exp 1.0 sat 1.0" and LUT_3D_SIZE 9, then 729 rows of three numbers between 0 and 1, red changing fastest. The same profile and settings give the same file byte for byte. A profile without "kind": "log-to-display-profile" answers {"error": "The profile must be an object with \"kind\": \"log-to-display-profile\"."} and exit 2.
